_about: Set free, side by side (plan 7.6b): wordings of fear and its end, of anxiety, of shame, and of bondage and release that more than one book shares, from the Exodus to the Gospels and the letters, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme's own outline cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.title: Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom; walk in freedom, live in freedom

Psalms & wisdom: And I will walk in freedom, for I have sought Your precepts.
The letters: where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
Be careful, however, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak.
For why should my freedom be determined by someone else's conscience?
to spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus, in order to enslave us.
For you, brothers, were called to freedom; but do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh.
Speak and act as those who are going to be judged by the law that gives freedom.
Live in freedom, but do not use your freedom as a cover-up for evil; live as servants of God.

rows.alike: Most speak of freedom as something to walk or live in, or to guard: 'I will walk in freedom' (Psalm 119:45), 'Live in freedom' (1 Peter 2:16), 'called to freedom' (Galatians 5:13), 'our freedom in Christ Jesus' (Galatians 2:4).
rows.different: Psalm 119:45 joins it to 'for I have sought Your precepts'; 2 Corinthians 3:17 says 'where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom'; Galatians 2:4 speaks of those who 'spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus, in order to enslave us'; 1 Corinthians 10:29 asks 'why should my freedom be determined by someone else's conscience?'; and Galatians 5:13, 1 Peter 2:16 and 1 Corinthians 8:9 each add a caution: 'do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh', 'do not use your freedom as a cover-up for evil', 'that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak'. James 2:12 speaks of 'the law that gives freedom'.

rows.title: Be strong and courageous; do not be afraid or discouraged

The Law & history: Do not be afraid or discouraged.
Be strong and courageous; do not be afraid or terrified of them
Be strong and courageous, for you will go with this people into the land
Do not be afraid or discouraged.
Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the Israelites into the land
Have I not commanded you to be strong and courageous?
Above all, be strong and courageous!
Do not be afraid or discouraged.
Be strong and courageous, for the LORD will do this to all the enemies you fight.
be strong and courageous, for though Saul your lord is dead
Do not be afraid. Have I not commanded you? Be courageous and valiant!
Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged.
Be strong and courageous, and do it. Do not be afraid or discouraged
Do not be afraid or discouraged because of this vast army
Do not be afraid or discouraged.
Be strong and courageous! Do not be afraid or discouraged before the king of Assyria
Psalms & wisdom: Wait patiently for the LORD; be strong and courageous.
Be strong and courageous, all you who hope in the LORD.
The Prophets: Do not be afraid or disheartened
Be strong now; be very strong!
But now be strong, O Zerubbabel
Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.

rows.alike: Each tells someone to be strong or not to be afraid: 'Be strong and courageous', 'Do not be afraid or discouraged', 'Be strong, do not fear!' (Isaiah 35:4). Many give a reason with 'for': 'for the LORD will do this to all the enemies you fight' (Joshua 10:25, in Joshua's words), 'for there is a greater One with us than with him' (2 Chronicles 32:7).
rows.different: The speakers differ: the LORD to Joshua (Joshua 8:1; Deuteronomy 31:23), Moses to Joshua (Deuteronomy 31:7), David to Solomon (1 Chronicles 28:20), 'the LORD says' to 'all you people of Judah and Jerusalem' (2 Chronicles 20:15), Psalm 31:24 to 'all you who hope in the LORD', and Absalom to the young men he has ordered to strike Amnon down: 'Do not be afraid. Have I not commanded you? Be courageous and valiant!' (2 Samuel 13:28). Isaiah 35:4 goes on 'Behold, your God will come with vengeance'.

rows.title: Take courage

The Law & history: Take courage and be men, O Philistines!
Gospels & Acts: Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven.
Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.
Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.
But take courage; I have overcome the world!
Take courage! As you have testified about Me in Jerusalem, so also you must testify in Rome.
keep up your courage, because you will not experience any loss of life
So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me.
The letters: Be men of courage. Be strong.

rows.alike: Each says 'Take courage' or close to it ('Be men of courage' in 1 Corinthians 16:13), and many give a reason with it: 'your sins are forgiven', said to the paralytic (Matthew 9:2), 'It is I' (Matthew 14:27), 'I have overcome the world' (John 16:33), 'for I believe God' (Acts 27:25).
rows.different: Jesus says it in Matthew 9:2, 9:22, 14:27 and Mark 6:50, and in Acts 23:11 'the Lord stood near Paul' and said it. John 16:33 sets it after 'In the world you will have tribulation'. In Mark 10:49 'they' who called the blind man say 'Take courage!' and 'He is calling for you'; Acts 27:22 speaks of 'loss of life, but only of the ship' and 27:25 says 'take courage, men'; in 1 Samuel 4:9 it is said to the Philistines, 'Otherwise, you will serve the Hebrews'. 1 Corinthians 16:13 has 'Be men of courage', as 1 Samuel 4:9 has 'be men'.

rows.title: Do not be afraid: your prayer has been heard

The Law & history: Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he lies.
The Prophets: your words were heard, and I have come in response to them.
Gospels & Acts: Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard.
Cornelius stared at him in fear
Cornelius, your prayer has been heard

rows.alike: Each tells someone not to be afraid, or comes to one who is afraid, and gives as the reason that a voice or a prayer has been heard: 'God has heard the voice of the boy' (Genesis 21:17), 'your words were heard' (Daniel 10:12), 'your prayer has been heard' (Luke 1:13, Acts 10:31).
rows.different: What is heard differs, and each is said to one person: in Genesis 21:17, said to Hagar, 'the voice of the boy'; in Daniel 10:12, to Daniel, his words 'from the first day that you purposed to understand'; in Luke 1:13 to Zechariah and Acts 10:31 to Cornelius, a prayer. Luke adds 'Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son', and Acts 10:31 'your gifts to the poor have been remembered before God'.

rows.title: Touched, and told 'Do not be afraid'

The Prophets: Then he touched me, helped me to my feet
Do not be afraid, you who are highly precious
Gospels & Acts: Then Jesus came over and touched them.
Revelation: But He placed His right hand on me
Do not be afraid. I am the First and the Last

rows.alike: In each there is a touch and a person on the ground or shaking: 'my face to the ground' and 'he touched me' (Daniel 8:18), 'a hand touched me and set me trembling on my hands and knees' (Daniel 10:10), 'fell facedown in terror' and 'Jesus came over and touched them' (Matthew 17:6-7), 'fell at His feet like a dead man' and 'He placed His right hand on me' (Revelation 1:17). In Daniel 10, Matthew and Revelation the words that follow are 'Do not be afraid'.
rows.different: Daniel 8:18 has no 'Do not be afraid'; Daniel 10:19 adds 'Peace be with you! Be strong now', Matthew 'Get up', and Revelation 'I am the First and the Last'. The one who touches is 'the one with the likeness of a man' in Daniel 10:18 and 'Jesus' in Matthew 17:7.

rows.title: The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?

Psalms & wisdom: in God I trust. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
The LORD is on my side; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
The Prophets: I will strengthen you; I will surely help you
Do not fear, I will help you.
Do not fear, O Jacob, you worm, O few men of Israel. I will help you
Do not fear the scorn of men
Why should you be afraid of mortal man
Gospels & Acts: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul.
do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more.
The letters: The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?

rows.alike: Each speaks of not fearing, and many set it against people: 'I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?' (Psalm 56:4, Psalm 118:6, Hebrews 13:6), 'Do not fear the scorn of men' (Isaiah 51:7), 'Do not be afraid of those who kill the body' (Matthew 10:28, Luke 12:4). Isaiah 41:13 says 'Do not fear, I will help you.'
rows.different: In Psalms 56 and 118 the speaker says it of himself, and in Hebrews 13:6 'we say' it; in Isaiah 41 the LORD says to Jacob, 'I will help you'; Luke 12:4 says it to 'My friends', and Matthew 10:28 goes on 'Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell'. Hebrews 13:6 has 'The Lord is my helper' where Psalm 118:6 has 'The LORD is on my side'.

rows.title: Do not fear what they fear

The Prophets: Do not fear what they fear; do not live in dread.
The letters: Do not fear what they fear; do not be shaken.
Revelation: Do not fear what you are about to suffer

rows.alike: Isaiah 8:12 and 1 Peter 3:14 both say 'Do not fear what they fear'; Revelation 2:10 says 'Do not fear what you are about to suffer'.
rows.different: Isaiah 8:12 begins 'Do not call conspiracy everything these people regard as conspiracy' and ends 'do not live in dread'; 1 Peter 3:14 says first 'even if you should suffer for what is right, you are blessed' and ends 'do not be shaken'. Revelation 2:10 goes on 'the devil is about to throw some of you into prison to test you, and you will suffer tribulation for ten days'.

rows.title: Even the hairs of your head

The Law & history: not a hair of his head will fall to the ground
not a hair of your son's head will fall to the ground.
not a single hair of his will fall to the ground.
Gospels & Acts: Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from the will of your Father.
And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.
And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
Yet not even a hair of your head will perish.
not a single hair of your head will be lost.
you cannot make a single hair white or black

rows.alike: Each speaks of a hair, or a sparrow, kept or counted: 'not a hair of his head will fall to the ground' (1 Samuel 14:45), 'not one of them will fall to the ground apart from the will of your Father' (Matthew 10:29), 'not even a hair of your head will perish' (Luke 21:18).
rows.different: In 1 Samuel 14:45 the people say it to Saul of Jonathan ('As surely as the LORD lives'); in 2 Samuel 14:11 it is a vow, 'not a hair of your son's head will fall to the ground'; in 1 Kings 1:52 Solomon says it on a condition, 'If he is a man of character'. Only Matthew 10:30-31 and Luke 12:7 join it to 'So do not be afraid' and to 'the very hairs of your head are all numbered'. Acts 27:34 gives it as a reason to 'eat something': 'not a single hair of your head will be lost'. Matthew 5:36 uses 'a single hair' of swearing by one's head: 'you cannot make a single hair white or black'.

rows.title: Lie down with nothing to fear; no one to frighten them

The Law & history: you will lie down with nothing to fear
Psalms & wisdom: You will lie down without fear
When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet.
I will lie down and sleep in peace, for You alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety
The Prophets: they will be left to the flocks, which will lie down with no one to fear.
Jacob will return to quiet and ease, with no one to make him afraid.
Jacob will return to quiet and ease, with no one to make him afraid.
They will dwell securely, and no one will frighten them.
when they dwell securely in their land, with no one to frighten them.
each man will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree, with no one to frighten him.
with nothing to frighten them away
But they will feed and lie down, with no one to make them tremble.
the needy will lie down in safety

rows.alike: Each speaks of lying down, or dwelling, safe, most with no fear: 'you will lie down with nothing to fear' (Leviticus 26:6), 'You will lie down without fear' (Job 11:19), 'with no one to frighten him' (Micah 4:4), 'with no one to make him afraid' (Jeremiah 30:10).
rows.different: Leviticus 26:6 sets it beside 'I will give peace to the land'; Job 11:19 goes on 'and many will court your favor'; Proverbs 3:24 adds 'your sleep will be sweet'. Jeremiah 30:10 and 46:27 say it to 'Jacob My servant' and 'O Israel', Zephaniah 3:13 of 'The remnant of Israel', and Ezekiel 39:26 'in their land'; Micah 4:4 has 'each man will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree'. Psalm 4:8 says 'I will lie down and sleep in peace', and Isaiah 14:30 says of 'the needy' that they 'will lie down in safety'. Isaiah 17:2 uses the words of flocks in forsaken cities, and Nahum 2:11 of lions.

rows.title: Not a spirit of fear

The Prophets: for you will have no fear. Terror will be far removed
The letters: you did not receive a spirit of slavery that returns you to fear
For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
and free those who all their lives were held in slavery by their fear of death.
There is no fear in love, but perfect love drives out fear

rows.alike: Each speaks of fear taken away or not given: 'you will have no fear' (Isaiah 54:14), 'God has not given us a spirit of fear' (2 Timothy 1:7), 'perfect love drives out fear' (1 John 4:18).
rows.different: Romans 8:15 and Hebrews 2:15 join fear to slavery ('a spirit of slavery that returns you to fear', 'held in slavery by their fear of death'); Isaiah 54:14 joins it to being 'far from oppression' and 'In righteousness you will be established', and 1 John 4:18 to love, saying 'fear involves punishment'. Romans 8:15 says 'you', 2 Timothy 1:7 'us', and Hebrews 2:15 'those who all their lives were held in slavery'.

rows.title: Do not worry about your life

The Law & history: do not worry about them, for they have been found.
The Prophets: It does not worry in a year of drought, nor does it cease to produce fruit.
Gospels & Acts: do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear.
Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
And why do you worry about clothes?
Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself.
you are worried and upset about many things.
do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
why do you worry about the rest?
The letters: Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.

rows.alike: Each says not to worry, or speaks of worrying: 'do not worry about your life' (Matthew 6:25, Luke 12:22), 'It does not worry in a year of drought' (Jeremiah 17:8), 'Be anxious for nothing' (Philippians 4:6).
rows.different: Matthew and Luke ask 'Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?', and Matthew adds 'tomorrow will worry about itself'; Luke 12:22 is said 'to His disciples'. Philippians 4:6 pairs it with 'by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God'. Jeremiah says it of a tree, 'He is like a tree planted by the waters'; 1 Samuel 9:20 is about 'the donkeys you lost three days ago', 'for they have been found'; and in Luke 10:41 the Lord says to Martha 'you are worried and upset about many things'.

rows.title: Do not worry about what to say

The Law & history: I will help you as you speak, and I will teach you what to say.
The Prophets: Behold, I have put My words in your mouth.
Gospels & Acts: do not worry about how to respond or what to say. In that hour you will be given what to say.
do not worry beforehand what to say. Instead, speak whatever you are given at that time
do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.
So make up your mind not to worry beforehand how to defend yourselves.

rows.alike: Exodus, Jeremiah, Matthew and Mark speak of what to say being given: 'I will teach you what to say' (Exodus 4:12), 'I have put My words in your mouth' (Jeremiah 1:9), 'you will be given what to say' (Matthew 10:19), 'speak whatever you are given' (Mark 13:11). The four Gospel verses say not to worry about what to say or how to answer.
rows.different: In Jeremiah 1:9 the LORD 'touched my mouth' and puts 'My words in your mouth'; Exodus 4:12 follows 'Now go!'. The Gospel verses are about when 'they hand you over' (Matthew 10:19, Mark 13:11) and 'you are brought before synagogues, rulers, and authorities' (Luke 12:11). Mark adds 'for it will not be you speaking, but the Holy Spirit'.

rows.title: Cast your burden on the LORD; cast your anxiety on Him

Psalms & wisdom: Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you
When anxiety overwhelms me, Your consolation delights my soul.
Anxiety weighs down the heart of a man, but a good word cheers it up.
The Prophets: Say to those with anxious hearts
The letters: Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.

rows.alike: Psalm 55:22 and 1 Peter 5:7 both say 'Cast' and give a reason: 'He will sustain you', 'He cares for you'. Psalm 94:19, Proverbs 12:25 and Isaiah 35:4 speak of anxiety met by a word: 'Your consolation', 'a good word', 'Be strong, do not fear!'
rows.different: Psalm 55:22 says 'your burden' where 1 Peter 5:7 says 'all your anxiety', and Psalm 55:22 goes on 'He will never let the righteous be shaken'. Psalm 94:19 speaks to 'You' of 'Your consolation'; in Proverbs 12:25 'a good word' is not said to be anyone's in particular; Isaiah 35:4 gives 'Be strong, do not fear!' as a word to 'Say to those with anxious hearts', and goes on 'Behold, your God will come with vengeance. With divine retribution He will come to save you.'

rows.title: Let me never be put to shame

Psalms & wisdom: Do not let me be put to shame; do not let my enemies exult over me.
let me not be put to shame, for I take refuge in You.
let me never be put to shame; save me by Your righteousness.
O LORD, let me not be ashamed, for I have called on You.
May those who hope in You not be ashamed through me
In You, O LORD, I have taken refuge; let me never be put to shame.
I cling to Your testimonies, O LORD; let me not be put to shame.
May my heart be blameless in Your statutes, that I may not be put to shame.
let me not be ashamed of my hope.
The Prophets: but do not let me be put to shame.
The letters: I eagerly expect and hope that I will in no way be ashamed

rows.alike: Each asks or hopes not to be put to shame, and most give a ground with 'for' or 'that': 'for I take refuge in You' (Psalm 25:20), 'for I have called on You' (Psalm 31:17), 'that I may not be put to shame' (Psalm 119:80).
rows.different: The Psalms speak to 'You': 'my God', 'O LORD', 'O Lord GOD of Hosts'; Jeremiah 17:18 asks it in the same breath as 'Let my persecutors be put to shame'; Psalm 69:6 asks it for others, 'not be ashamed through me'; Philippians 1:20 is an expectation rather than a prayer, 'I eagerly expect and hope', joined to 'Christ will be exalted in my body, whether by life or by death'.

rows.title: Those who hope in Me will never be put to shame

Psalms & wisdom: Surely none who wait for You will be put to shame
Those who look to Him are radiant with joy; their faces shall never be ashamed.
In the time of evil they will not be ashamed
The Prophets: No longer will Jacob be ashamed and no more will his face grow pale.
you will not be put to shame or humiliated, to ages everlasting.
those who hope in Me will never be put to shame.
I know that I will not be put to shame.
Do not be afraid, for you will not be put to shame
For you will forget the shame of your youth
My people will never again be put to shame.
My people will never again be put to shame.
On that day you will not be put to shame for any of the deeds by which you have transgressed against Me.

rows.alike: Each says that someone 'will not be put to shame' or 'shall never be ashamed', and most name who: 'none who wait for You' (Psalm 25:3), 'Those who look to Him' (Psalm 34:5), 'those who hope in Me' (Isaiah 49:23), 'My people' (Joel 2:26).
rows.different: In Psalm 25:3, 34:5 and 37:19 the words are of 'none who wait for You', 'Those who look to Him' and 'they'; Isaiah 29:22 has the LORD speak 'of the house of Jacob'; in Isaiah 49:23, Joel 2:26-27 and Zephaniah 3:11 the LORD speaks in the first person ('I am the LORD', 'My people', 'against Me'); and Isaiah 45:17 says 'Israel will be saved by the LORD'. In Isaiah 50:7 the speaker says it of himself, 'Because the Lord GOD helps Me'. Isaiah 54:4 and Zephaniah 3:11 add what is put behind: 'the shame of your youth', 'the deeds by which you have transgressed against Me'.

rows.title: Ashamed, or not ashamed, of Me and My words

Psalms & wisdom: I will speak of Your testimonies before kings, and I will not be ashamed.
Gospels & Acts: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him
If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him
The letters: I am not ashamed of the gospel
So do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, or of me, His prisoner.
I am not ashamed; for I know whom I have believed
an unashamed workman who accurately handles the word of truth.
Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God
But if you suffer as a Christian, do not be ashamed, but glorify God that you bear that name.

rows.alike: Each speaks of being, or not being, ashamed of someone or something: 'I will speak of Your testimonies before kings, and I will not be ashamed' (Psalm 119:46), 'ashamed of Me and My words' (Mark 8:38, Luke 9:26), 'I am not ashamed of the gospel' (Romans 1:16).
rows.different: In Hebrews 11:16 it runs the other way: 'God is not ashamed to be called their God'. Mark 8:38 and Luke 9:26 begin 'If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words' and go on 'the Son of Man will be ashamed of him'; 2 Timothy 1:12 and 1 Peter 4:16 join it to suffering, 'even though I suffer as I do' and 'if you suffer as a Christian'.

rows.title: May those who seek my life be put to shame

Psalms & wisdom: All my enemies will be ashamed and dismayed
Let the wicked be put to shame
May those who seek my life be disgraced and put to shame
may those who exalt themselves over me be clothed in shame and reproach.
May those who seek my life be ashamed and confounded
May those who seek my life be ashamed and confounded
May the accusers of my soul be ashamed and consumed
that my enemies may see and be ashamed
When they rise up, they will be put to shame, but Your servant will rejoice.
May all who hate Zion be turned back in shame.
I will clothe his enemies with shame
The Prophets: all who rage against you will be ashamed and disgraced
But they will be put to shame.
Let my persecutors be put to shame
they will be utterly put to shame, with an everlasting disgrace that will never be forgotten.
The letters: so that anyone who opposes us will be ashamed, having nothing bad to say about us.
so that those who slander you may be put to shame by your good behavior in Christ.

rows.alike: Each speaks of shame falling on those who oppose: 'May those who seek my life be ashamed and confounded' (Psalm 40:14), 'all who rage against you will be ashamed and disgraced' (Isaiah 41:11), 'those who slander you may be put to shame' (1 Peter 3:16).
rows.different: In the Psalms and Jeremiah it is mostly a wish ('May...', 'Let...') and sometimes a statement (Psalm 6:10, Jeremiah 20:11); Psalm 132:18 and Isaiah 41:11 state it, and Isaiah 66:5, 'the word of the LORD' to 'You who tremble at His word', says 'But they will be put to shame.' In Titus and 1 Peter it comes about through 'wholesome speech that is above reproach' and 'by your good behavior in Christ'.

rows.title: A slave to sin; I will not be mastered by anything

Gospels & Acts: everyone who sins is a slave to sin.
The letters: that we should no longer be slaves to sin.
you are slaves to the one you obey, whether you are slaves to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness
though you once were slaves to sin
For when you were slaves to sin, you were free of obligation to righteousness.
sold as a slave to sin.
but I will not be mastered by anything.
enslaved to all sorts of desires and pleasures
They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves to depravity. For a man is a slave to whatever has mastered him.

rows.alike: Each speaks of being a slave to sin or to what masters a person: 'everyone who sins is a slave to sin' (John 8:34), 'you are slaves to the one you obey' (Romans 6:16), 'a man is a slave to whatever has mastered him' (2 Peter 2:19).
rows.different: Romans 6:17 says 'you once were slaves to sin', Romans 6:20 'when you were slaves to sin' and Titus 3:3 'at one time we too were' enslaved, while Romans 6:6 says 'we should no longer be slaves to sin'; Romans 7:14 says 'I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin'; 2 Peter 2:19 says it of those who 'promise them freedom'; and 1 Corinthians 6:12 sets 'I will not be mastered by anything' beside 'Everything is permissible for me'.

rows.title: Set free from sin; free indeed

Gospels & Acts: Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.
So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.
The letters: For anyone who has died has been freed from sin.
You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.
But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves to God
set you free from the law of sin and death.
It is for freedom that Christ has set us free.

rows.alike: Each says 'set you free', 'set free from sin' or 'freed from sin': 'the truth will set you free' (John 8:32), 'if the Son sets you free' (John 8:36), 'You have been set free from sin' (Romans 6:18), 'Christ has set us free' (Galatians 5:1).
rows.different: What sets free is named differently: 'the truth' (John 8:32), 'the Son' (John 8:36), 'the law of the Spirit of life' (Romans 8:2), 'Christ' (Galatians 5:1); Romans 6:7 says it of 'anyone who has died'. Romans 6:18 and 6:22 add what follows: 'slaves to righteousness', 'slaves to God'.

rows.title: No longer a slave, but a son

Gospels & Acts: A slave does not remain in the house forever, but a son remains forever.
The letters: as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave
we were enslaved under the basic principles of the world.
So you are no longer a slave, but a son; and since you are a son, you are also an heir through God.
no longer as a slave, but better than a slave, as a beloved brother.

rows.alike: Most set 'slave' beside 'son', 'child' or 'brother': 'A slave does not remain in the house forever, but a son remains forever' (John 8:35), 'no longer a slave, but a son' (Galatians 4:7), 'no longer as a slave, but better than a slave, as a beloved brother' (Philemon 1:16).
rows.different: John 8:35 speaks of 'the house'; Galatians 4:1 and 4:3 speak of a child, 'no different from a slave' and 'enslaved'; Romans 8:15 and Galatians 4:6 join sonship to the cry 'Abba! Father!' and 'Abba, Father!'; Galatians 4:7 adds 'an heir through God'; Philemon 1:16 says 'no longer as a slave' of one 'especially beloved to me, but even more so to you'.

rows.title: Out of the house of slavery; you were slaves in Egypt

The Law & history: out of the house of slavery
out of the house of slavery.
out of the house of slavery.
so that you would no longer be slaves to the Egyptians
out of the house of slavery.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt
out of the house of slavery.

rows.different: The settings differ: the LORD's own words 'I am the LORD your God' (Exodus 20:2, Deuteronomy 5:6); an answer to a son's question (Exodus 13:14) and what 'you are to tell him' (Deuteronomy 6:21); the reason for a command, 'Therefore I am commanding you to do this' (Deuteronomy 24:22), or for the Sabbath (Deuteronomy 5:15); a warning, 'be careful not to forget the LORD' (Deuteronomy 6:12); and an order to put to death 'a prophet or dreamer' who 'has advocated rebellion against the LORD your God' (Deuteronomy 13:5).
